fullPassage: The customary starting point for economic theory, the basic model to which other situations and policy options are compared, is a system of perfectly competitive markets. This imagined economy is populated exclusively by small producers and individual consumers, all possessed of very broad information and very narrow motives and desires. In such an economy, under long lists of traditional but unrealistic assumptions, economists have proved that there is always an "equilibrium" — that is, a set of prices at which supply equals demand for every commodity. The invisible hand of market competition, in Adam Smith's famous metaphor, ensures that every resource is used wherever it will produce the greatest value for consumers. Any deviation from the free-market outcome will make someone worse off, so there is no possible change to a market equilibrium that could win unanimous support.

③ ← 정답: 'a set of prices at which supply equals demand for every commodity' — 균형은 공급=수요인 가격 집합
④ cost determines value: 비용이 가치를 결정한다는 내용은 본문에 없음. 불일치
det.tip: equilibrium = 공급(supply)과 수요(demand)가 일치(equals)하는 상태.

Any deviation from the free-market outcome will make someone worse off, so there is no possible change to a market equilibrium that could win unanimous support.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 ①~④ 중, 원문과 다른 것은?

det.korean: ① very broad motives and desires → very narrow motives and desires: 원문에서 정보(information)는 broad이지만, 동기와 욕구(motives and desires)는 narrow. 대비 구조를 이용한 오류
det.analysis:
✅ ① very broad motives(오류): 원문은 'very broad information and very narrow motives and desires' — information은 broad, motives와 desires는 narrow. broad로 바꾼 것은 원문 불일치 ← 정답
❌ ② traditional but unrealistic assumptions: 원문 그대로
❌ ③ a set of prices at which supply equals demand for every commodity: 원문 그대로
❌ ④ every resource is used wherever it will produce the greatest value for consumers: 원문 그대로
det.tip: broad information ↔ narrow motives. 대비(contrast) 구조에 주의.
